headline: P0022 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 26.2% is about 3.6x the 7.2% expected for its patient mix, and the excess persists in every complexity stratum
rationale: This panel is sicker than average: 10 of the 16 99215s fall on patients with 4 or more chronic conditions, and only one sampled 99215 is on a low-complexity patient (C0011177, hyperlipidemia with an abdominal-pain code). Patient complexity does not explain the full gap, though. The 99215 share is 26.2% against 7.2% expected given complexity (z = 3.18, risk-adjusted score 2.17). It runs about two to three times the all-provider rate within each stratum: 2 conditions 14.3% vs 5.6%, 3 conditions 26.7% vs 8.7%, 4 conditions 33.3% vs 13.9%, 5+ conditions 66.7% vs 29.8%. No 99211 or 99212 visits were billed at all. Several sampled high-complexity 99215s list only one chronic code or an acute, minor or follow-up code, such as rash, URI or a Z09 follow-up (C0011120, C0011139, C0011168, C0011152). One patient, P0022-N0014, accounts for four of the sampled 99215s (C0011119, C0011136, C0011139, C0011169). Together this is a pattern consistent with upcoding layered on a genuinely complex panel, but it is not conclusive. Stratum counts are small (6 to 18 visits), the claim lists are samples, and no clinical documentation, MDM or time records are in the packet.
next_steps: Request and review medical records for the sampled 99215s, starting with C0011177, C0011120, C0011139 and C0011168, to check whether the documented MDM or total time supports level 5.
Pull the full claim set, not just samples, to confirm the within-stratum excess, given the small stratum counts (e.g. 6 visits with 4 conditions).
Review all visits for patient P0022-N0014 to see whether the repeated 99215s reflect acute exacerbations or routine follow-up.
Compare documentation for 99214 visits on similar patients (e.g. C0011124, C0011127 for the same patients as some 99215s) to see what distinguishes the levels.
Check whether the absence of any 99211/99212 billing reflects the visit types actually furnished.
